title: finding(plugin-grid): the server-side export path sends `sort: []` when every entry was filtered out, instead of omitting the key — the "question with no content" shape `toFilterNode` already corrected for `$filter`
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01VCpmqvacV4BypY48QdoxcE`, R1, 2026-09-16T10:3xZ, from the `## Acceptance notes` of PR #9604 (card objectui#8961). ⛔ Not claiming; grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's.

**Filed rather than left in the PR body because it is the one residual there with no successor.** The seat's rule is that an acceptance note is only a valid resting place when a specific PR or person will touch that code — 「说得出具体 PR 或人 ⇒ 写进去」. The reporting dev recorded **「Successor: none queued」** in as many words for this item, so the note would have had no reader. Its sibling note (a stale verbatim quotation in `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`) **does** name a successor and is correctly staying in the PR body — ⛔ not filed.

## The observation

`ObjectGrid`'s **server-side export path** filters an array of retired string `sort` entries down to an **empty array** and still sends `sort: []` to `exportDownload`, rather than omitting the key.

⇒ the request carries an ordering instruction that names no ordering — a question with no content.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a shrug

⭐ **The same shape has already been ruled on and corrected one key over.** `toFilterNode` corrects exactly this for `$filter`: a predicate that reduces to nothing is **omitted**, not sent as an empty container. So this is not a new judgement call about what is tidy — it is one consumer of a settled local convention that did not get the treatment.

⚠️ It is also the **residue of the defect objectui#8961 just fixed**, one layer down. #8961 narrowed the header-arrow reader so a retired string spelling lights no arrow, matching a fetch path that already refused it. The export path filters the same retired entries out — and then still transmits the empty result. The two readers of `sort` now agree about the arrow; the *third* consumer still emits a degenerate value.

## ⛔ What is NOT claimed

- ⛔ **Not claimed that the server mishandles `sort: []`.** That was not measured, and it is the reading that sets the priority: if an empty array and an absent key are treated identically end to end, this is a p3 tidiness item; if they diverge (a default ordering applied in one case and not the other), it is a user-visible defect. **Whoever grades this should take that reading first** — it is in objectstack, not here.
- ⛔ Not claimed to be new or introduced by PR #9604. It is **pre-existing** and unrelated to the arrow; PR #9604 neither created nor touched it. Measured and reported by that PR's dev while in the file, ⛔ not fixed there, correctly — it is outside that card's declared surface.
- ⛔ Not claimed to be reachable except through the retired spelling: an author writing the declared `[{ field, order }]` array is unaffected.
